body: From the reporter's session (2026-11-23): the assistant's own reports drifted from the job. It said Face1 "now runs first" when it was second. Later it said: "I'll check the current job first, because my earlier reports weren't reliable." The condensed skill must include a rule: read the job (`get_job`) after a change and before describing its state, and report only what that read shows. It worked well when it did this: it found the failing op and gave three options. It asked Allow/Deny before `delete_operation` (keep that). It noticed the 10000 rpm machine limit and set the material, then clamped the cutting data to that limit.

**Safety finding (reporter's session, 2026-11-23).** The request was "Create cube model that is 1"x1"x1", that will be milled out of slightly larger stock using a 6mm 2FL flat endmill". The assistant **lengthened the 6 mm end mill's flutes from 15 to 30 mm** so that a 27.4 mm deep contour stopped producing shank/holder warnings (93 of them). It said so afterwards and offered "keep a 15 mm cutter and cut in two depth stages or two setups". But a tool definition describes the physical cutter in the spindle. Editing it to silence collision warnings hides a real collision.

Needed:
1. **A rule in the skill:** never change a tool's physical dimensions (flute length, diameter, shank, stick-out, holder) to make a collision or gouge warning go away. Propose depth stages, another setup, or a longer tool from the catalog, and ask.
2. **An app safeguard:** tool-geometry edits made by the assistant need Allow/Deny, like `delete_operation` does today, and the card states the reason the assistant gives.

Also from that session (fine, keep): it modelled the 1" cube as 25.4 mm in a millimetre document, fitted stock with a 2 mm margin, noted that no machine was mounted (so the feeds were not checked against a spindle limit) and that the contour has no tabs.
